subject: Post-call: FastRetail performance qualification and benchmark instructions
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Meera Shah <meera.shah@fastretail.com>, benchmark@fastretail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps: performance targets & prompt inventory request

Hi Meera / FastRetail team — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap plus concrete next steps so we can scope the qualification run and share a reproducible harness.

Recap (from our notes):
- Primary objective: qualify Redwood Dedicated for your storefront generation pipeline (autocomplete + short response flows).
- Priority SLOs: low p95 latency for short completions, predictable concurrency bursts during promotions, and support for streaming partial outputs for UX snappiness.
- Data controls: customer-owned VPC option + request to redact any PII before logs are stored.

Action items we need from FastRetail to build the run plan: 
1) Target latency SLOs: please confirm p50/p95 targets for both short (<=50 tokens) and long (~>200 tokens) responses. If you only have one target today, tell us which traffic tier to prioritize.
2) Concurrency profile: typical sustained qps and expected burst size (peak qps during promotions).
3) Streaming requirements: do you require time-to-first-token (TTFT) guarantees vs only final response latency? Any constraints on partial output frequency (e.g., commit a token every X ms)?
4) Prompt inventory: sample prompt set (anonymized) and a small labeled set (~50 examples) of expected completions so we can reproduce quality and token counts. A CSV or JSONL is fine.

What we'll deliver once we have the above:
- A documented benchmark harness (Docker + runbook) that reproduces loads and collects TTFT, p95/p99 tail latencies, tokens/sec, and memory/KV cache utilization.
- An initial calibration run and a short-readout with plots and a table of fail/pass vs your target SLOs.
- A proposal for any configuration changes (batching, quantization profile, autoscale thresholds) and a recommended rollout plan.

Attachments: SLO_matrix.xlsx (proposal template), prompt_inventory_v1.csv (example format). Please replace samples with sanitized customer data.

Proposed schedule: if you can share prompt samples and targets by COB Wed 19 Aug, we can schedule the calibrations w/c 24 Aug and aim to have a readout by 26 Aug.

Questions for you now: what date works for the calibration window (Aug 24–26)? Also confirm whether procurement should coordinate any contract/PO steps in parallel (cc'ed: Tom?).

Thanks — looking forward.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0142

From: Meera Shah <meera.shah@fastretail.com>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:43:22 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: performance targets & prompt inventory request

Hi Diego — thanks for the clear summary. Confirming the high-level targets and adding details below so you can build the harness.

Targets:
- Short flows (search-ish/autocomplete, median completion ~30 tokens): p50 <= 35ms, p95 <= 150ms.
- Long flows (end-to-end answers, avg ~220 tokens): p50 <= 450ms, p95 <= 1200ms.
- TTFT: we prefer streaming with TTFT <= 50ms for short flows; for long flows TTFT <= 120ms.

Concurrency and traffic shape:
- Typical sustained: ~40 requests/sec across our primary region (US-west).
- Peak (promotions): spikes up to ~300 req/sec for 2–10 minute windows, with heavy token fanout for some templates.

Quality constraints and redaction:
- We will provide sanitized prompt samples. Please ensure your harness can run with our PII redaction enabled. We will not send raw customer PII — you can process sanitized examples.

Attachments: customer_prompt_samples.csv (50 anonymized prompts). We're also adding an ops alias (benchmark@fastretail.com) to receive any large payloads.

Calibration note: we would like a short calibration run with identical prompt seeds before a full qualification so we can baseline any noise from networking / warm caches. Does Redwood support deterministic seeding for the same model variant (token-level deterministic seeds)?

Tom — looping you in for procurement cadence if we proceed after the qualification readout.

Best,
Meera Shah
Engineering Manager, ML Systems | FastRetail Inc.
meera.shah@fastretail.com

Attachments: customer_prompt_samples.csv (CSV stub)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Meera Shah <meera.shah@fastretail.com>, benchmark@fastretail.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps: performance targets & prompt inventory request

Thanks Meera — this is exactly the level of detail we need. A few clarifications and what we'll configure on our side to keep the runs reproducible: 

Measurement definitions we will use (to avoid ambiguity):
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): measured at the service ingress from request timestamp to the time the first token byte is emitted on the response stream.
- Final response latency: measured from ingress to the time the final token is committed to the response stream. We will report p50/p95/p99 for both TTFT and final-latency.
- Concurrency handling: we distinguish concurrent requests (simultaneous in-flight inference calls) vs token throughput (tokens/sec generated across all workers). Our harness will allow you to specify steady-state concurrent clients and burst arrival patterns (Poisson, step).
- Deterministic seeding: we can pin RNG seed for a chosen model variant and run with identical prompt seeds — this will make exact token sequences reproducible for calibration runs. Note: seeding reproducibility can vary with quantization and kernel scheduling; we'll note that in the readout.

Proposed harness config for the calibration run:
- Model variant: rwd-13B-quant-8 (suggested starting point). If you prefer a 7/8-bit profile let us know — we will note accuracy vs perf tradeoffs.
- Batch size profile: auto-batching with max batch 32 for short flows; we'll create a separate stream for long flows with a lower max batch (8) to keep TTFT low.
- Warmup: 300 sample requests to stabilize KV cache and JIT kernels (we'll run warmup on the same node pool).
- Metrics we will collect: TTFT (per-request), final latency, tokens emitted per second, GPU util, memory footprint, KV cache hit ratio, and a sample of response content for QA.

Deliverables we will share after the calibration: readout slides (plots + SLO table), raw harness logs (gzipped), and a short README with exact Docker command lines and the prompt seed file so you can reproduce locally.

Next steps: Marissa / Soojin — can you confirm the proposed model variant and the quant profile to try first? Also flag any infra constraints (VPC egress rules, KMS) we should be aware of before the 24–26 Aug window. If all good, we'll schedule the calibration for Tue 25 Aug 09:00 PT (1 hour block) and reserve the slot.

Diego
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

I'll own the run and the post-run plots. We'll attach the raw logs and the SLO_matrix.xlsx filled with measured values after the run.

Thanks — Soojin
